content:
We need to find the correct template ID and mapped_rxn that reproduces the precursors list when applied to target molecule. The search returned several templates; we need to identify which one matches silylation of alcohol with TBDMSCl.

Look at template 182479: retro_smarts_template seems complex, not simple silylation. Template 145718: retro_smarts_template '[C:4]=[C:3]-[C:2]-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-[Si](-C)(-C)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2]-[C:3]=[C:4]'. That is protection of allylic alcohol? It converts an alkene with OH to silyl ether attached to carbon chain. Not exactly our case (our target has an OH attached to a carbon that is part of a cyclic acetal? Actually target has O[Si] attached to a carbon in a sugar-like ring. The OH is on a carbon attached to OSi group. The template may be generic: converts C-OH to C-O-SiR3. The template 145718 seems plausible: it takes a carbon chain with OH attached to a carbon (maybe secondary alcohol) and adds Si group.

But we need to see if applying this template to target yields the precursors list (which includes the same molecule but with OSi group? Wait target already has OSi group. The precursors list includes the same molecule (with OSi) and the silyl chloride. That suggests the retrosynthetic step is to disconnect the silyl ether, giving the alcohol (without Si) and the silyl chloride reagent. However the listed precursors still have OSi in the first entry (same as target). Actually first precursor list entry: ["C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO","Cl[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C"] The first SMILES still has O[Si] group. That seems like the product (target) unchanged. Maybe the apply_template step gave multiple possible precursors, some of which are the same as product (i.e., no change) due to alternative mapping? Not sure.

Nevertheless, we need to return mapped_rxn and template_id used to generate those precursors. Likely template_id is 145718 (from search result). Let's retrieve full template info to get mapped_rxn. Use get_template with ID 145718.
